questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Having always wanted to experience the american college culture first-hand, I felt compelled to go to a school in the US. Having a whole town of only college students around the university really helped the case for choosing UCSB in specific; while I did want the quintessential college experience, I still wanted to be in California, where I could (somewhat) easily go to SF or LA for shows or friends.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: People, both at my home university, and the university i was an exchange student at were incredibly helpful. Every time I had a problem that I needed additional information for, I would write a short message or email, and I would get accurate help very fast.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since I was lucky enough to live in student housing, the whole process of picking up keys and move-in times was a bit confusing to me at first. After a short email correspondence, I was all set.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not super easy - I got lucky and got off-campus housing through the university. My best recommendation would be to apply early, and perhaps with a friend.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Get a bike! They are super cheap if you get them at the impounded bike sale at the beginning of the school year ($20). Also living off campus is probably your only bet, but luckily everything is very close.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Get ready to pay upwards of $1000 to share a single room with 1-2 other people.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You would have certain pass times. When it was your pass time, you would simply log onto the website that was used for course registration (GOLD), and there you would select your class and the section time you wanted to attend (given that there were more available spaces)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In the case you couldn't register for courses, you could email or book consultations with different people in the respective departments.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all courses besides one. I had a problem with prerequisites not aligning perfectly, but after discussing it with 3-4 different people, it went to the chair of the department and then i was approved by my professor in the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Email, email, email. Book consulting, do it early and be consistent (to the point where you might be a little annoying)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did a couple of upper-division courses, but I did not delve into MA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures were much shorter, and there was a bigger focus on sections.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Music Appreciation, Introduction to Astronomy, Machine Learning.
Emerging Adulthood, Introduction to Human Sexuality, Programming Languages.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Human Sexuality. It was such a fun class. It was taught by an old couple that had a lot of knowledge to share. Despite the topic being a little odd, it was super insightful, and you learn a lot of things that you would never learn in standard sex-ed (even for european standards)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: This was not really an unexpected cost, but the structure was unexpected. When you live in student housing, you pay rent for 3 months instead of doing it monthly.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beer and meat was a bit expensive. Costco Rotisserie Chicken was cheap, and so was their hotdog.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was part of the climbing team - it was super fun

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty much every sport you can think of. However, there was no american football. There was also a bunch of different clubs - meditation club, korean christian societies, and of course greek life.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sports club, and perhaps a club with a focus on work. By doing that you develop a strong network in the US

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Red Rocks (Nevada), Santa Cruz, San Luis Obispo, Los Angeles, San Francisco and Yosemite were some really fun trips. Hawaii is also great during thanksgiving - if you have no one to spend it with, you might as well enjoy an incredibly beautiful state.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took me 1 months to adjust to everything. This is rather slow, but I found small unexplainable differences in culture that i was unable to ignore for some reason. After the first month it was a bunch of fun.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people. Everyone is super open, and really interested in your "exoticness"

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People being very friendly off the get-go.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People being very friendly off the get-go.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Have fun, 2. Befriend the locals, 3. Look for unusual opportunities that are available in the US but not back home. In my case, an unusual opportunity was djing at local college bars.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not everyone will accept a danish drivers license as a valid ID

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Building relations all over the state. Of course, there has been a bunch of atomized experiences that I really enjoy, but I believe I will look back on my exchange with much fondness of all the people I met and befriended.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning to be more honest with everyone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
